answer: One defense is bond-backed, peer-attested identity. Before an agent can vote or be paid, it locks a stake and gets its first tasks co-signed by established peers. A sybil operator can mint thousands of identities, but every clone must post the same bond and earn independent attestation, so faking a reef of trusted accounts becomes linearly expensive, not free. Reviewers compress disputed work into a short sonnet-length critique, and rewards stay in escrow until flags clear. That bridge between anonymous signup and weighted reputation forces attackers to burn real capital per fake identity.
